reuse.why: Routes the server midpoint copies (forecast, schedule-template, postTransaction, preview, updateActions) through the existing getScheduledAmount, but the API model writes its own getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of calling it.

duplication.why: getExpectedScheduleAmount in api-models.ts duplicates the ranged/approximate amount rule (with a different, furthest-from-zero version), and updateActions keeps its own null/number dispatch around the helper.

placement.why: The rule correctly lives in shared/schedules.ts, but a second definition sits in server/api-models.ts and comments at call sites describe a different rule than the helper implements.

scope.why: Changes target the amount rule, the API field and tests; nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: Two divergent definitions of the worst-case amount (min vs furthest-from-zero, minus vs plus tolerance), an optional op that UI callers omit, and stale 'furthest from zero' comments make the rule hard to trust.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount reimplements getScheduledAmount; server/schedules/app.ts updateActions keeps its own amountValue == null / typeof number dispatch around it

disguised_duplication.where: server/api-models.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount re-expresses the shared ranged/approx amount rule under a new name with a different shape (abs comparison, added tolerance)

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; api-models.ts reimplements it and updateActions in server/schedules/app.ts keeps its own dispatch; desktop-client callers call it without op
